column1: # Gaps of the 'multicast' block that are no longer gaps, keyed to the same
# 'killed' means a mutation taken from this sweep's output now fails a test.
# 'equivalent' means the mutation is real and the program is the same either way.
# 'superseded' means the line the verdict belongs to was replaced by a fix.

column6: why

HostName is not null && Port.HasValue in IsResolved, with ||. Both are set in one place, Apply's SRV case at 921 and 922, and always together; nothing unsets either. So they are null together or set together, and && and || agree

UnicastResponseRequested = false on the record's primary constructor. Every caller passes it: the parser from the QU bit it read, the constructor at line 70 from its own parameter, and the suite's two direct callers go through that one. The default the browser's questions go out on is line 70's, and the querier tests kill it there
offset <= wire.Length in RData, with <. They differ where the RDATA is empty, and wire.AsMemory(offset) is then the empty memory the mutant returns

length > 0 && bitmap[length - 1] == 0 as Encode trims a window, with >=. A window is made only for a type in it, so its bitmap holds a set bit, and the loop stops at that bit before length reaches zero, where the mutant would read bitmap[-1]

ExpiresAt > Now ? ExpiresAt - Now : TimeSpan.Zero in RemainingTimeToLive, with >=. They differ where ExpiresAt equals Now, and the mutant's ExpiresAt - Now is then TimeSpan.Zero, the original's answer

offset + 2 <= TypeBitMaps.Length in Decode, with <. They differ where exactly two octets are left. The original reads them as a window and a length and stops at the next test, since no bitmap follows: a length of zero breaks, and any other runs past the end. The mutant stops before. Neither adds a type

remaining > TimeSpan.Zero in IsKnownAnswerAt, with >=. RemainingTimeToLive is never negative, so the mutant's conjunct is always true. The original's is true for every entry that gets here: each caller reads the clock and then takes its entries from CachedRecords, which reads it again and keeps only those with ExpiresAt after that second reading. That is the client's KnownAnswers at 1042 and the browser's QueryNowAsync and ObserveQuery, which read it at 367 and 421. An entry with no time left at the first reading would need a clock that ran backward between two readings of one synchronous call
bit < 8 in Decode, with <=. The ninth pass tests 0x80 >> 8, which is zero, and adds nothing

maxDelay > minDelay ? minDelay + a random share of the difference : minDelay, with >=. They differ where the two are equal, and the share is then of a zero difference, FromTicks((Int64) (x * 0)): minDelay either way. The draw the mutant adds comes from Random.Shared, which is not seeded, so nothing that draws after it can tell

SetSocketOption(IP, PacketInformation, true) on the IPv4 socket, with false. Socket.ReceiveMessageFromAsync turns the option on itself before it receives: planted, the transport still reported the interface and the group as the destination of every multicast, and both come from the packet information

if (delay > TimeSpan.Zero) around the first query's delay, with >=. They differ at a delay of zero, which the mutant awaits. Task.Delay(TimeSpan, TimeProvider, CancellationToken) answers a cancelled token with a cancelled task and a delay of zero with a completed one, and creates no timer for either. The first ends the loop at the catch's return, where the original ends it at the while's test of the same token. The second goes on at once, as the original does

new MemoryStream(buffer, false) in TryParse, writable with true. Nothing writes to the stream: DNSTools.ExtractName and DNSInfo.ReadResourceRecord only read names and records off it, and the class bits are cleared in the buffer through its span, not through the stream
interval > MaxBrowseInterval as the browse interval doubles, with >=. They differ where the two are equal, and the mutant then sets the interval to the value it has
SetSocketOption(IPv6, PacketInformation, true) on the IPv6 socket, with false. The same as line 222, for IPv6

info.IPv6Addresses.Count > 0 && info.IPv6Index.HasValue, choosing the interfaces to join FF02::FB on: with || and with >= 0. SelectInterfaces asks for an interface's IPv6 index only when it has IPv6 addresses (line 583), so HasValue implies the count, and the count without the index would need GetIPv6Properties to fail for an interface that has IPv6 addresses

info.IPv6Addresses.Count > 0 && info.IPv6Index.HasValue, choosing the interfaces to join FF02::FB on: with || and with >= 0. SelectInterfaces asks for an interface's IPv6 index only when it has IPv6 addresses (line 583), so HasValue implies the count, and the count without the index would need GetIPv6Properties to fail for an interface that has IPv6 addresses

remaining < interval ? remaining : interval, with <=. The two differ only where remaining and interval are equal, and then both pick the same TimeSpan; the comparison at 560 sees the same wait. The line it replaced, 490 at 925c80d5, was the same and was left open there

changed && SRV && HostName is not null before the cached addresses of the instance's host are applied, with the second && made ||: (changed && SRV) || HostName is not null. The mutant applies them also when an unchanged SRV record or a TXT record arrives for an instance with a host, and discards what Apply returns, as the original does. Every cached address of the host is among the instance's by then: an address that arrives is applied to every instance on its host (586), a host is given its cached addresses the moment an SRV record names it (571, 650, and ApplyCached at 837), and an address leaves the instance only as it leaves the cache (664, 678). Apply adds nothing
grace > Options.ResponseGracePeriod before a lookup's grace period, with >=. They differ where the two are equal, and the mutant then sets grace to the value it already has

question.Name.Serialize(stream, offset, false, null) in Serialize, compressing with true. Serialize then makes a dictionary of its own (Offsets ??= []) for each question, and compresses a name only where the whole name is in it already; one name never finds itself there before it is written, so each question is written in full, as the original writes it

question.ExpiresAt <= now as SendQueryAsync prunes the recent unicast questions, with <. The mutant keeps a question that expires at that very moment. Nothing reads the list but IsExpectedUnicastResponse, which prunes it again with <= at its own reading of the clock, no earlier than this one, before it looks; the catch at 641 removes only the call's own registrations

info.Index == InterfaceIndex.Value || in SendAsync's filter, with &&, which binds before the || around it: (Index == X && IPv4Index == X) || IPv6Index == X. Index is IPv4Index where there is one and IPv6Index where not, so Index == X makes one of the two sides true, and either side makes the original true

if (goodbyeRecords.Length > 0) before an update's goodbye, with >=. With nothing to say goodbye to, the mutant calls SendGoodbyeAsync with an empty list, and Split yields no packet for it: the loop has nothing to run over, and the last yield asks packetAnswers.Count > 0 || packetAdditionals.Count > 0, which two empty lists answer with no. Nothing awaits on the way, so no cancellation can tell either

the `true` SizeOf hands Query as Truncated, while it measures how long a packet would be. Serialize turns Truncated into one bit of the header's third octet (MulticastDNSMessage.cs:596) and into nothing else: the header is twelve octets either way, and the sections are written alike. The packets that go out are built at 702, with a TC bit of their own

info.IPv4Index == InterfaceIndex.Value || in SendAsync's filter, with &&: Index == X || (IPv4Index == X && IPv6Index == X). It differs only for an interface whose IPv4 index is not its IPv6 index, and the operating systems .NET runs on give an interface one index for both

lifetime > TimeSpan.Zero before the query at 80 %, with >=. They differ where the lifetime is zero, and the conjunct after it is then remaining < 0 * (1 - RefreshFraction), which no RemainingTimeToLive satisfies: it is never negative

SizeOf(current) > Options.MaxQuerySize, with >=. A known answer that fills a packet to the octet is closed into a group of its own at once, where the original keeps it as the open group. Nothing can join it: every record adds octets, so the next one overflows that group at 678, and the original closes it there, as it was; if none follows, 699 closes it. The groups come out the same. The method run over abstract sizes, every list of up to five known answers drawn from nine sizes under three limits and three question sizes, 597,870 cases, gave no difference here. It gave one for each of the five survivors on 671 to 699 that stay open: 671's ==, 678, both of 683 and 699
info.IPv6Addresses.Count > 0 before multicasting over IPv6 on an interface, with >= 0. The index that follows it has a value only where the count is above zero, as at line 271
entry.ExpiresAt > now + 1 s in §10.2's flush, with >=. They differ where an entry expires exactly one second from now, and the mutant then sets its expiry to that same time
existing.ExpiresAt > now + GoodbyeDelay in §10.1's goodbye, with >=. They differ where the record expires exactly then, and the mutant sets that same time

Apply's return false for a record none of its cases match, with true, since finding 93's fix (c5b4ce08). Every caller that reads the result hands Apply records chosen by the comparison its case then makes again: an SRV or TXT record by the instance key at 559, the preferred SRV record from the cache by the instance's name at 565 and 648, an address by SameName at 587. The key and SameName fold as DNSServiceName.Equals does now, so each record meets its case. The callers that hand it anything else, ApplyCached at 832 and 835 and the address loops at 571 and 848, discard the result. At 0f595ac4 the key folded É to é, and two instance names that differ in its case reached the line; the planted mutant survives the Multicast project's 117 tests at c5b4ce08

ours.CompareLexicographically(theirs) < 0 in §8.2's tie-break, with <=. They differ where the two sets compare equal: as many records, and pairwise the same class, type and rdata. Both sets are of one name, the group's, so each of theirs is then identical to one of ours, and the check just above it has already gone on to the next name for exactly that case

ipv4Addresses.Count > 0 before asking for the IPv4 index, with >= 0. An interface without IPv4 addresses then gets an IPv4 index, which is its IPv6 index, and nothing uses it: there are no IPv4 addresses to join or send from, and its subnets, all IPv6, never match an IPv4 source
ipv6Addresses.Count > 0 before asking for the IPv6 index, with >= 0. The same as line 580, for an interface without IPv6 addresses

Record.TimeToLive > ttlOverride.Value, the legacy unicast cap of §6.7, with >=. They differ where a record's TTL equals the cap, ten seconds, and then the override the mutant sets is the TTL the record has. The wire carries the same ten either way
PrefixLength < 0 || PrefixLength > length in bits, with &&, which is never true. The guard is for prefix lengths outside the address, and no interface reports one
PrefixLength < 0, with <= 0. It differs for a prefix of length zero, which no interface address has
return false for a prefix length outside the address, with true. No interface reports one, as at line 643

packetAnswers.Count > 0 || packetAdditionals.Count > 0, Split's last yield, with >= in either place. The mutant yields where both lists are empty, and they are empty there only when Split was handed two empty lists. No caller hands it any: PublishAsync and UpdateAsync refuse a publication without records, the query path returns before it when it has no answers and again when the rate limit leaves none, and an update's goodbye is sent only when it has records (750)

packetAnswers.Count > 0 || packetAdditionals.Count > 0, Split's last yield, with >= in either place. The mutant yields where both lists are empty, and they are empty there only when Split was handed two empty lists. No caller hands it any: PublishAsync and UpdateAsync refuse a publication without records, the query path returns before it when it has no answers and again when the rate limit leaves none, and an update's goodbye is sent only when it has records (750)

if (Max <= Min) return Min in RandomDelay, with <. They differ where the two are equal, and the mutant then returns Min plus a random share of a zero difference: Min either way. The draw comes from Random.Shared, which is not seeded
